transcript: So you think you're ready to create your first paid course? Awesome. In this video, I'm going to walk you through exactly how I created my first paid online course, which has now gone on to generate over seven figures in sales. So you can learn from my mistakes and you can shortcut your way to success. So let's dive right in. The very first question you need to ask yourself is, what's my course about? Who am I helping and what problem am I solving for them? And if you don't have a clear answer to that question, then you need to stop watching this video and you need to go and figure that out first, because without that, you have no business creating a course. Now, for me, when I started my business, I was creating a course for people who wanted to learn how to create a website with WordPress. That was something I was doing for clients on the side, and I was really good at it. And people were constantly asking me to teach them how to do it. So I knew there was a market for it. The next thing you need to figure out is, is there a market for this? Like, who are your dream students? What problems are they facing? What results do they want? And what are the solutions that you're going to provide them with inside of your course? Now, there's a lot of different ways you can validate your course idea. You can do surveys, you can do polls, you can talk to people, you can go to forums, you can go to Facebook groups. For me, because I already had clients, I already knew there was a market for it. People were already asking me to teach them how to do it. So for me, the validation process was fairly simple. But for you, if you're starting from scratch, then you need to put in the work and you need to make sure that there's a market for your course. And once you've done that, then it's time to build your content outline. Now, the content outline is essentially the entire structure of your course, all the modules, all the lessons, all the topics you're going to cover. Now, for me, when I created my first course, I decided to take my clients from absolute beginner to actually launching their very first website. So I started with teaching them how to choose a domain name and web hosting, how to install WordPress, how to install a theme, how to customize the theme, how to add content, how to add pages, how to add posts, how to add images, how to add videos, how to build out their menu, how to add a contact form, and then how to launch their website and promote it. That was my course outline. Now, your course outline is going to be different depending on your niche and your topic. But the key thing here is to make sure that you're taking your students from point A to point B. And once you've got your content outline, then it's time to create your content. Now, there's a lot of different ways you can create your content. You can do video, you can do audio, you can do text, you can do slides, you can do screen shares. For me, because I was teaching people how to build a website, the most logical way was to do screen shares. So I would literally record my screen and show people exactly what to click, what to type, what to do. Now, there are a few tools that I use to create my content. The first tool I use is called Camtasia. It's a screen recording software, and it's fantastic for recording your screen and editing your videos. The second tool I use is a microphone. Now, you don't need a fancy microphone. You can start with a headset mic, or you can start with a USB mic. I started with a USB mic, and it worked perfectly fine. And then the third thing you need is a good camera. Now, again, you don't need a fancy camera. You can start with your iPhone. I started with a webcam, and it worked perfectly fine. The key thing here is to make sure that your audio is clear and your video is clear. And once you've got your content created, then it's time to build out your course platform. Now, there are a lot of different course platforms out there. You can use Thinkific, you can use Teachable, you can use Kajabi, you can use LearnDash, you can use Sensei. For me, because I was teaching people how to build a website with WordPress, the most logical solution was to use a WordPress plugin called LearnDash. Now, LearnDash is a fantastic course plugin for WordPress, and it allows you to create your courses, manage your students, track their progress, and even issue certificates. Now, it does cost a little bit of money, but it's totally worth it if you're serious about building a professional course platform. Now, once you've got your course platform built out, then it's time to upload your content. So you're going to upload all your videos, all your audios, all your text, all your slides, and you're going to organize them into modules and lessons. And once you've done that, then it's time to set up your pricing. Now, there are a lot of different ways you can price your course. You can do a one-time payment, you can do a recurring subscription, you can do a payment plan. For me, I decided to do a one-time payment because it was my first course, and I wanted to make it as simple as possible for people to buy. Now, the price point you choose is going to depend on your niche, your topic, and the value you're providing. For me, I started with a price point of $197, and it worked perfectly fine. Now, once you've set up your pricing, then it's time to set up your sales page. Now, the sales page is essentially the page where people are going to go to learn about your course and decide whether or not they want to buy it. And on your sales page, you want to make sure you have a compelling headline, a clear explanation of what your course is about, who it's for, what problems it solves, what results it provides, testimonials, case studies, frequently asked questions, and a clear call to action. Now, there are a lot of different ways you can build your sales page. You can use a page builder like Elementor, you can use a WordPress theme, or you can use a dedicated sales page builder like ClickFunnels. For me, I used Elementor, and it worked perfectly fine. Now, once you've got your sales page built out, then it's time to promote your course. Now, there are a lot of different ways you can promote your course. You can do email marketing, you can do social media marketing, you can do paid advertising, you can do affiliate marketing, you can do joint ventures. For me, I started with email marketing because I already had an email list. So I sent out a series of emails to my email list, and I promoted my course. And then I also used social media marketing. I posted about my course on Facebook, on Instagram, on Twitter, and I also did some paid advertising. I ran some Facebook ads to promote my course. Now, the key thing here is to make sure that you're promoting your course to the right audience. You want to make sure you're targeting people who are interested in your topic and who are likely to buy your course. And once you've promoted your course, then it's time to launch it. Now, the launch process is essentially the period of time where you're actively promoting your course and trying to get as many sales as possible. And during your launch, you want to make sure you're providing a lot of value, you're answering questions, you're overcoming objections, and you're building excitement. Now, for me, my first launch was a huge success. I generated over five figures in sales in my first launch. And then over time, my course went on to generate over seven figures in sales. And it's all thanks to following these steps. Now, if I were to start all over again today, there are a few things I would do differently. The first thing I would do differently is I would focus more on building an audience before launching my course. When I first launched my course, I only had a small email list. And if I had a bigger email list, I would have generated even more sales. So I would recommend focusing on building an audience through content marketing, through social media, through YouTube, through podcasting, whatever it is, focus on building an audience first. The second thing I would do differently is I would create a smaller, more focused course. My first course was a fairly comprehensive course. It covered everything from start to finish. And if I were to start all over again today, I would create a smaller, more focused course that solves a very specific problem. And then I would create additional courses that solve additional problems. The third thing I would do differently is I would focus more on building a community around my course. When I first launched my course, I didn't have a community. And I think that's a huge missed opportunity. A community allows your students to connect with each other, to ask questions, to get support, and to feel like they're part of something bigger. So I would definitely recommend building a community around your course. And the fourth thing I would do differently is I would focus more on getting testimonials and case studies from my students. When I first launched my course, I didn't have any testimonials or case studies. And I think that's a huge missed opportunity. Testimonials and case studies are incredibly powerful for social proof, and they help new students decide whether or not they want to buy your course. So I would definitely recommend focusing on getting testimonials and case studies from your students. And I'm going to share with you all the things I've learned from generating over seven figures in sales from my own online courses. So if you're ready to create your first paid online course, then click the link below and join the free training. I'll see you there.

sections.heading: 첫 유료 강의 제작을 위한 핵심 질문: 주제와 타겟 문제 정의
sections.body: 첫 유료 온라인 강의를 제작하기 전 가장 먼저 스스로에게 던져야 할 필수적인 질문은 강의의 주제가 무엇인지, 내가 누구를 돕고자 하는지, 그리고 그들에게 어떤 구체적인 문제를 해결해 줄 것인지다. 이러한 질문들에 대해 명확하고 투명한 답변을 내놓을 수 없다면 강의 제작을 즉시 멈추고 이를 먼저 정립해야만 한다. 화자는 자신의 경우 WordPress로 웹사이트를 제작하는 법을 가르치는 강의로 시작했는데, 이는 이미 클라이언트들에게 전문적으로 제공하던 서비스였기에 확신을 가질 수 있었다. 사람들이 끊임없이 자신에게 가르쳐달라고 요청하는 분야를 선택함으로써 시장의 실제적인 니즈를 확인한 것이다. 결국 성공적인 강의의 출발점은 자신의 전문성과 시장의 고충이 교차하는 지점을 정확히 짚어내는 데서 시작된다.
highlights: 가장 먼저 스스로에게 던져야 할 필수적인 질문은 강의의 주제가 무엇인지, 내가 누구를 돕고자 하는지, 그리고 그들에게 어떤 구체적인 문제를 해결해 줄 것인지다.
이러한 질문들에 대해 명확하고 투명한 답변을 내놓을 수 없다면 강의 제작을 즉시 멈추고 이를 먼저 정립해야만 한다.
sections.quote: The very first question you need to ask yourself is, what's my course about? Who am I helping and what problem am I solving for them?

sections.heading: 시장 검증: 드림 스튜던트의 니즈와 솔루션 일치
sections.body: 강의 주제가 정해졌다면 다음 단계로 해당 분야에 실제로 구매력이 있는 시장이 존재하는지 철저히 검증해야 한다. 당신이 꿈꾸는 이상적인 학생들(dream students)이 누구인지 정의하고, 그들이 현재 겪고 있는 고통과 그들이 궁극적으로 얻고 싶어 하는 결과가 무엇인지 분석해야 한다. 강의 내에서 제공할 솔루션은 이러한 타겟 학생들의 요구 사항과 정확히 일치해야 하며, 그들의 문제를 해결할 수 있는 실질적인 방안을 담고 있어야 한다. 시장 검증은 단순히 추측에 의존하는 것이 아니라 실제 데이터와 예비 학생들의 피드백을 통해 객관적으로 이루어져야 한다. 화자는 이미 기존 클라이언트들로부터 시장성을 확인했기에 이 과정이 수월했지만, 초보자에게는 가장 많은 공을 들여야 하는 단계다.
highlights: 강의 주제가 정해졌다면 다음 단계로 해당 분야에 실제로 구매력이 있는 시장이 존재하는지 철저히 검증해야 한다.

sections.quote: The next thing you need to figure out is, is there a market for this? Like, who are your dream students?

sections.heading: 실전 강의 아이디어 검증 방법론: 설문과 커뮤니티 활용
sections.body: 강의 아이디어를 검증하기 위한 구체적인 방법으로는 설문조사, 투표, 잠재 고객과의 직접적인 대화, 관련 포럼이나 페이스북 그룹 활용 등이 있다. 화자의 경우 이미 서비스를 이용하던 클라이언트들이 가르쳐달라고 요청하는 상황이었기에 시장 검증 절차가 매우 단순하고 확실했다. 하지만 아무런 기반 없이 처음부터 시작하는 제작자라면 직접 발로 뛰며 자신의 강의를 구매할 시장이 존재하는지 반드시 확인하는 노력을 기울여야 한다. 검증 없이는 강의 제작에 들인 시간과 노력이 낭비될 위험이 크기 때문에, 실제 수요를 확인하는 작업은 선택이 아닌 필수다. 이러한 시장의 니즈가 최종적으로 확인된 후에야 비로소 본격적인 콘텐츠 아웃라인을 작성하는 단계로 넘어갈 수 있다.
highlights: 강의 아이디어를 검증하기 위한 구체적인 방법으로는 설문조사, 투표, 잠재 고객과의 직접적인 대화, 관련 포럼이나 페이스북 그룹 활용 등이 있다.
이러한 시장의 니즈가 최종적으로 확인된 후에야 비로소 본격적인 콘텐츠 아웃라인을 작성하는 단계로 넘어갈 수 있다.
